questions.question: What problem does Docker primarily solve for Python data applications?
options: It makes Python code run faster by using compiled containers
It packages the application with all its dependencies so it runs identically on any machine
It automatically deploys applications to the cloud
It replaces virtual environments for managing Python packages
questions.explanation: "It works on my machine" is a classic engineering problem. Docker containers bundle your code, Python version, all packages, and system dependencies into an image that runs identically everywhere—your laptop, a teammate's Windows PC, or a cloud server. This eliminates environment-related bugs.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Docker image and a Docker container?
options: Images are for Linux; containers are for Windows
An image is a read-only blueprint; a container is a running instance of that image
Images store data persistently; containers are temporary caches
A container is multiple images merged together
questions.explanation: A Docker image is a static snapshot—the recipe. A container is a live, running process created from that image. You can run multiple containers from the same image simultaneously, each isolated. This is analogous to a class (image) vs. instance (container) in Python OOP.

questions.question: In a Dockerfile, what does the `COPY . .` instruction do?
options: Creates a copy of the Docker image
Copies files from the current host directory into the container's working directory
Copies files between two containers
Duplicates the base image layer
questions.explanation: `COPY <src> <dest>` copies files from the build context (your local machine) into the image. `COPY . .` copies everything from the current directory (`.`) to the current working directory inside the container (also `.`). This is how your application code gets into the image.

questions.question: What does `docker run -p 8000:8000 my-api` accomplish?
options: Builds the image and runs it 8000 times
Starts a container from 'my-api' and maps host port 8000 to container port 8000
Creates 8000 replicas of the container for load testing
Runs the container for exactly 8000 seconds
questions.explanation: The `-p host_port:container_port` flag publishes a container's port to the host. Without port mapping, the container's network is isolated and unreachable. `-p 8000:8000` makes the API running inside the container accessible at `localhost:8000` on your machine.

questions.question: Why should you install Python dependencies in the Dockerfile before copying your application code?
options: Dependencies must always be installed first due to Python import rules
Docker caches each layer—installing dependencies first means the slow step is cached and only re-runs when requirements.txt changes
It prevents the application code from overwriting installed packages
Docker requires alphabetical ordering of instructions
questions.explanation: Docker builds images layer by layer and caches unchanged layers. If you copy code before installing dependencies, every code change invalidates the dependency layer and triggers a full `pip install`. Copying `requirements.txt` first and installing before copying code means `pip install` only re-runs when dependencies actually change—rebuilds are much faster.
